title: Style rules in the card
summary: Measured on 178 cards with run transcripts on agent-runner-01 (21 October to 3 November 2026): the frontend area of the prompt-enrichment selector fires on 97% of cards with 35% precision, the frontend-styling guide reached 1 of 45 frontend cards because two optional slots are filled in id order, 19 of 45 frontend cards opened none of the style sources, projects without docs/quality received no style rule, and review verdicts cannot cite rule ids. implementationTasks.title: Rule-pack format and catalogue
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/style-rule-delivery/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md when UI is involved, docs/quality/README.md, docs/quality/adding-a-rule.md and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-3465 Dossier (style rules in the card). Use the Dossier's recommended option for every decision (D1-B, D2-B, D3-B, D4-C, D5-A, D6-B, D7-B, D8-B, D9-B, D10-A) unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

Dependencies: none. Resolve slice ids to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

## Goal
Make rule packs in skill format a first-class catalogue source next to the existing style guides, without changing selection yet.

## Scope
- Discover project packs at `docs/quality/rules/<pack>/SKILL.md` (bounded: at most 64 packs, 32 KiB per SKILL.md, deterministic path order, no symbolic or reparse paths) and workspace packs from a product-shipped `rule-packs/<pack>/SKILL.md` folder.
- Frontmatter: `name` (pack id, lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, at most 64), `description` (at most 600), and a `metadata` map with string values: `pack-version`, `tier` (`binding` or `guidance`), `applies-to` (inline JSON with `projects`, `technologies`, `surfaces`, `paths` globs, `taskKinds`, same OR semantics and explicit `*` as `appliesTo` today), optional `keywords`.
- Body: a `## Binding rules` list where each item starts with a rule id (`[A-Z]{2,5}-[0-9]+`) and ends with `Check: <lint:id | test:Name | review>`. Rule ids are unique across the catalogue; a duplicate id, a duplicate pack id between workspace and project, an invalid glob, or more than 12 binding rules excludes the pack with a relative-path warning.
- Expose packs, rules and warnings in the existing style-guide catalogue snapshot and API with the same snapshot id semantics. Existing top-level guides keep loading unchanged.
- Document the format in docs/quality/README.md and docs/quality/adding-a-rule.md, and add the rule-pack folder row to docs/start/README.md.

## Out of scope
Selection, prompt rendering, delivery, review.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fixture packs (project and workspace) parse into packs with rules, tiers, globs and checks; unit tests cover each rejection reason.
- The three existing guides still load with unchanged ids and snapshot behaviour.
- The catalogue API returns packs and warnings without repository roots.
- docs/quality/README.md, adding-a-rule.md and docs/start/README.md describe the format.

implementationTasks.title: Rule selection v5 and tiered budget in pre-prompt-enrichment
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/style-rule-delivery/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md when UI is involved, docs/quality/README.md, docs/quality/adding-a-rule.md and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of the AGT-3465 Dossier (style rules in the card). Use the Dossier's recommended option for every decision (D1-B, D2-B, D3-B, D4-C, D5-A, D6-B, D7-B, D8-B, D9-B, D10-A) unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

Dependencies: S1. Resolve slice ids to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

## Goal
Select rule packs from strong deterministic signals and render binding rules in full inside the existing Prompt enrichment step, with every omission visible.

## Scope
- Signals in order of strength: (1) pins: new card field `rulePacks`, orchestrator pins, and the existing pipeline-type `EnrichmentBlockIds`; (2) inheritance: a review-fix or continuation card takes the source card's delivered packs and the packs matched by the source card's diff file list (source facts); (3) repository paths and Angular component selectors named in the authored prompt and in referenced Dossiers and cards, matched against pack `paths` globs (build a selector-to-path index from `selector: 'app-...'` declarations); (4) earlier-attempt diff for reissues; (5) pack keywords with word boundaries, at least two distinct hits; (6) card mode gate: coding and review-fix receive binding rules, concept cards receive the pointer index only unless a pack is pinned.
- Tiered budget inside the existing 6,000-character ceiling: tier 0 mandatory platform blocks; tier 1 binding rules in full (at most 12 rules and 1,200 characters per pack, 4,000 characters total); tier 2 guidance packs as one-line pointers (at most 6). Order by signal strength, then by narrowest glob; never by id. Overflow drops pointers before binding rules.
- The launch context and `intake/enriched-context.md` list omitted packs with the reason; `enrichment-report.json` gains a `rulePacks` section (pack id, version, digest, signal, rule ids delivered, omitted rule ids, reason) and keeps the existing fields. The pipeline step summary reads `<n> packs, <m> binding rules, <k> omitted`.
- Keep `AreaNeedles` and the C# blocks for non-pack candidates until S6. Selector tokens stay zero.

## Acceptance criteria
- Replay tests from the Dossier: a card naming `frontend/src/app/features/quota/components/header-quota/...` receives `header-zone`; a review-fix card of that card inherits it; a backend-only prompt containing the words card, lane and build receives no Angular pack; with angular-components, dotnet-backend and frontend-styling all eligible, frontend-styling is no longer dropped by id order.
- An overflow fixture shows the omitted pack in the prompt, the context file and the report.
- Report and step record zero selector tokens; the enriched prompt stays at or below 6,000 characters.
- docs/system/domains/pipeline.md and docs/quality/README.md describe the selection order and budget.

Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

Dependencies: S3. Resolve slice ids to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

## Goal
Make the selected rules visible in the card's Docs and present for local and remote runs, including the full pack references, without writing into the worktree.

## Scope
- Write `rules/selected-rules.md` into the task folder in the same atomic sequence as the enrichment report (context, document, then report as commit marker). It lists delivered packs with their binding rules, pointers, omitted packs with reasons, and the snapshot id. The Docs tab (prompt-pane, tab id `description`) lists it.
- Add an additive `RuleDelivery` object to `RunSpecDto` on the monolith and the standalone Task Server claim paths: document markdown plus the selected pack files (SKILL.md and references), each with path and SHA-256, bounded to 64 KiB in total; older runners ignore it.
- The runner materializes the packs into the per-card clean-context skill root before CLI start: `$CODEX_HOME/skills/<pack>/` for Codex and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/<pack>/` for Claude Code, replacing packs from an earlier round of the same card and leaving the `.system` and plugin skills untouched. It also writes the document to the run's job-docs location used for local runs.
- Never write pack files into the worktree.

## Verification
The CLI behaviour changes, so run a live probe per installed CLI on a runner (Claude Code and Codex at their installed versions) that asks the CLI to list its skills with a materialized probe pack, and record the result in results/. Claude Code `.claude/skills` and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills` discovery was not verifiable during the concept run (authentication), so this probe is required.

## Acceptance criteria
- The Docs tab of a task lists rules/selected-rules.md; a Playwright spec covers it with light and dark screenshots.
- A remote run receives RuleDelivery and the materialized packs; an older runner without support still runs with the prompt-only rules.
- The live probes show the probe pack in the skill listing of both installed CLIs; results/ holds the transcripts.
- `git status --porcelain` in the run worktree shows no pack file after materialization.

Read docs/style-rule-delivery/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md when UI is involved, docs/quality/README.md, docs/quality/adding-a-rule.md and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. Dependencies: S3. Resolve slice ids to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

## Goal
Check each delivery against exactly the rules the agent received, cite rule ids, and record selection misses.

## Scope
- New aspect step `aspect-rule-fit` in the review library with the standard pipeline-step settings (enabled state, prompt override, CLI, model, thinking level; default the bounded support aspect route). Schedule it only when the delivered packs from `enrichment-report.json` or the packs matched by the merge-base diff paths contain rules with `Check: review`.
- Frozen prompt: the delivered binding rules with ids, the diff-matched packs that were not delivered (marked as such), and the authoritative diff material. It reuses the cached common prefix of the stock aspects.
- Extend the verdict sentinel with `rules_cited=<comma-separated rule ids>`; a block without a rule id and a diff location becomes concerns under the existing citation policy. Rules with a deterministic check are not judged by the model; when their gate failed, the aspect cites the failed gate.
- Record per card: delivered rules, cited rules, verdict per rule, and selection misses (diff-matched pack not delivered).
- Update docs/system/domains/review.md (aspect list, sentinel, scheduling).

## Acceptance criteria
- A fixture delivery that renders a header destination twice yields a block citing the matching HDR rule and a file and line.
- An uncited block is downgraded to concerns; a guard-checked rule is not judged by the model.
- A diff touching header-zone paths on a card without the pack records a selection miss and still reviews the pack.
- The grade report shows cache read tokens for the new aspect on the shared prefix.

implementationTasks.title: Rule ledger and proposed rule cards
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/style-rule-delivery/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md when UI is involved, docs/quality/README.md, docs/quality/adding-a-rule.md and docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html. Git handling stays with the platform: do not commit, push or manage worktrees yourself.

Dependencies: S5. Resolve slice ids to promoted task keys before starting dependent work.

## Goal
Turn rule-cited findings and repeated uncited findings into proposed rule work.

## Scope
- Ledger on the Task Server: one entry per rule-fit verdict per rule (rule id, pack version, card, verdict, delivered or not, finding summary, diff location).
- Triggers, evaluated after each settled review: a delivered rule cited on two cards within 14 days proposes a sharpen-rule card; a cited rule that was not delivered proposes a surface-map card for the pack globs; two uncited findings in one pack's paths within 14 days propose a new-rule card; a rule cited three times whose finding is mechanical proposes a guard card.
- Proposed cards land in the project backlog through the Task API, carry the ledger evidence and link docs/quality/adding-a-rule.md; a trigger never proposes a second open card for the same rule.
- Show the ledger per pack on the pack's Wiki page or the Deck quality view (read-only).

## Acceptance criteria
- Two seeded citations of one delivered rule within 14 days propose exactly one sharpen-rule card.
- A cited undelivered rule proposes one surface-map card; an existing open card suppresses a duplicate.
- The ledger is visible read-only per pack.
